disposition_reason: The original volume-decoding task and Table 1 90-channel PopT+BrainBERT result are identifiable, including all seven downstream participants. Exact historical rows, ranked channel ensembles and checkpoint/feature binding are still unqualified. The existing support-disjoint prospective RMS evaluator cannot stand in for the paper’s random-row task.

source_paper.title: Population Transformer: Learning Population-level Representations of Neural Activity

evidence.locator: Section 4; Table 1; Appendix A Downstream Training; Appendix C Volume; Appendix D Table 6
evidence.supports: Original volume endpoint, 90-channel ROC-AUC baseline, subject aggregation, training recipe and downstream recording cohort.

evidence.locator: Fine-tuning section; data.write_multi_subject_multi_channel and run_train.py routes
evidence.supports: Author BrainBERT-feature extraction, checkpoint and saved-split route exists; exact historic artifacts are not authenticated.
Source downstream row splits use train_test_split with random_state=42 and separate saved split identities.
Pins the downstream subject/trial pairs without reading labels.
Defines 2048-Hz Laplacian neural inputs and five-second context around words.
Native ROC-AUC uses sklearn roc_auc_score; rounded-probability F1 is a separate diagnostic.

evidence.locator: Figure 3, Volume panel horizontal axis and legend
evidence.supports: The original electrode-count conditions are 1, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50; curves compare pretrained PopT, non-pretrained PopT, Linear and Deep NN. Exact curve ordinates were not digitized.

target.description: Binary word-volume decoding on the paper’s original Volume endpoint: distinguish top versus bottom RMS-intensity quartiles within each recording. This original endpoint is within the registration’s volume/speech/sentence scope; a result claims this endpoint only. Retain the original Volume electrode-count analysis alongside the 90-electrode Table 1 primary.

dataset.description: The original BrainTreebank intracranial movie recordings and word/audio annotations used for Table 1. Pin exact source-release and derived feature manifests before execution; a newer corpus version cannot silently replace them.

cohort.description: All seven source downstream pairs: sub_1/trial001, sub_2/trial006, sub_3/trial000, sub_4/trial000, sub_6/trial004, sub_7/trial000, sub_10/trial000. Table 6 identifies their held-out movies; three share Cars 2.

split.description: Original downstream train/validation/test proportions are .8/.1/.1, using random row splits and saved identities. Exact original word/feature row order and saved membership are not authenticated. Replacing them with the local support-disjoint split creates an extension.

inputs.description: Table 1 Volume comparison uses 90 clean Laplacian electrodes per participant with the original BrainBERT temporal embeddings and coordinates; preserve identical feature/checkpoint access and channel-ranking policy. A smaller ensemble is not the Table 1 task. Figure 3 Volume additionally uses the original 1, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 electrode conditions; the local 1/10/50/90 grid is not their replacement.

preprocessing.description: Author source specifies Laplacian rereferencing, 2048 Hz and five-second neural context; paper Appendix C defines per-word RMS with frame length 2048 and hop 512 and extreme-quartile labels. Exact feature timing, original ranked channel membership/order, ties, transcript alignment and native class mapping still need artifact-level reconciliation.

metric.description: Within each participant compute ROC-AUC, equivalently P(score_positive>score_negative)+0.5 P(tie), then source aggregation. Higher is better. F1 and local PopT-minus-linear gains do not replace the absolute PopT source score.

aggregation.description: Table 1 reports the mean ROC-AUC across source participants with standard error across subjects; for Volume, BrainBERT+pretrained PopT is 0.87 ± 0.03 at 90 channels. Preserve participant weighting, not pooled words.

comparison.primary_metric: Table 1 Volume ROC-AUC, BrainBERT inputs, 90 electrodes, mean across seven subjects

published_baseline.description: Table 1 pretrained PopT with BrainBERT: Volume ROC-AUC 0.87 ± 0.03 SEM across subjects, using 90 channels. The linear aggregation 0.66 ± 0.03 is a weaker comparator and beating it is not a paper win.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Pinned author extraction, saved-split and fine-tuning routes exist; the original BrainBERT/PopT checkpoint-feature identities, ranked channels, saved row memberships and numeric rerun are not authenticated.

minimum_effect.rationale: Choose a meaningful ROC-AUC improvement only after exact author calibration and examination of participant-level variability; a gap over the weak linear comparator is not the required effect.

uncertainty.method: Predeclare a paired candidate-versus-author analysis on the complete seven-subject panel with repeated seed effects separated and within-recording temporal dependence plus shared-movie dependence retained. Exact joint uncertainty rule is unresolved.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Subject with recording-time clustering; shared movie stimulus is a dependence factor, not seven independent movie replications.
uncertainty.rationale: Published subject SEM is descriptive. Resampling individual words as independent or counting overlapping neural contexts would overstate precision.

paper_win_requires: Bind the original 90-electrode Table 1 Volume task for all seven participants, including source random-row partitions, labels, BrainBERT features and pretrained access.
Exceed 0.87 published subject-mean ROC-AUC and a calibrated matched pretrained-PopT rerun by a justified predeclared effect with uncertainty.
Freeze candidate after original training/validation development and before complete original test scoring.
Report new chronological/support-disjoint splits, fewer electrodes, alternate tasks or narrowed participants as extensions; none establishes Table 1 victory.

Retain the Figure 3 Volume analysis at all original 1, 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 electrode counts and its four source comparator curves; recover numerical curves and predeclare how count effects constrain the claim. The 90-electrode primary does not license omitting registered electrode-count effects.

current_sota.description: The source-paper comparison is distinct from current SOTA; no current-SOTA search or claim is admitted by this contract.

episode.improvement_loop: After historical binding, use the original training/validation rows for candidate development; train-only channel ranking must be reconciled with the historical recipe rather than silently changed.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze candidate, feature/checkpoint provenance, all seven word rosters/splits, 90-channel membership/order, class mapping, training seeds and metric policy before test access.
episode.final_evaluation: Evaluate complete original test rows with author ROC-AUC per subject and source mean aggregation; retain shared-stimulus and temporal uncertainty. Report the complete original Figure 3 Volume electrode-count conditions and comparators alongside the 90-electrode primary.
episode.baseline_policy: The stronger-than-paper comparator is pretrained PopT+BrainBERT at 90 channels. Linear/deep concatenation baselines remain calibration controls; new support-disjoint evaluation is separately labeled extension. Where the source protocol itself uses stochastic draws, a faithful rerun may use declared provenance, a justified reproduction tolerance and paired candidate-author draws; fixed source partitions and full original condition support must remain unchanged.

blocking_issues: Exact original row order, saved .8/.1/.1 memberships and ranked 90-channel membership/order are unauthenticated.
Native audio/brain alignment, quartile ties, class orientation and feature/checkpoint content identity require qualification.
Author pretrained-PopT rerun, compatible working evaluator, fixed episode budgets, meaningful effect and joint uncertainty remain absent.
Pretraining exposure includes downstream subjects; trial disjointness is not unseen-subject or unseen-movie evidence.
Original Figure 3 Volume curve values and ranked ensembles at 1/10/20/30/40/50 electrodes need recovery; no digitized plot ordinates are treated as a rerun.

legacy.notes: Retain the prospective RMS evaluator and engineering controls. Its support-disjoint split, 1/10/50/90 nested grid and paired PopT-versus-linear gain are calibration/extension outputs. They are not reproduction or victory on Table 1’s original 90-channel random-row evaluation.
